title: Specialty Espresso Bar
sources: Specialty Coffee Association (SCA) Barista Skills Standard
World Barista Championship Official Rules & Standards
Barista Hustle Espresso Compass & Milk Texturing Framework
rules: Espresso extraction ratio must stay between 1:1.8 and 1:2.2 for standard brew recipes
Milk must be aerated early in the steaming cycle (below 37°C / 100°F) before vortex integration
Dairy milk serving temperature must stay between 60°C and 65°C to preserve sweetness without denaturing proteins
Steam wands must always be purged before and wiped/purged after every milk cycle
assumptions: Room layout is a 20x13 tile specialty coffee workspace with accessible back counter and pass-through bar
Water filtration is tuned to 130-150 ppm TDS and 93°C boiler temperature
Player navigates between grinder, espresso machine, milk station, and service pass

stations.name: Dosing & Grinder Bench
stations.description: Weigh portafilter, adjust burr micron setting, grind, distribute, and tamp coffee bed levelly.

stations.name: Dual-Boiler Espresso Machine
stations.description: Flush grouphead, lock portafilter, pull shot under 9 bars, monitor yield and extraction time.

stations.name: Milk Steaming Station
stations.description: Select milk pitcher, aerate microfoam, swirl vortex, monitor temperature, and purge wand.

stations.name: Cold Storage & Pitcher Rinser
stations.description: Store whole milk, oat milk, cold brew supplies, and chilled stainless steel pitchers.

stations.name: Handover & Service Counter
stations.description: Assemble final drinks with latte art, attach lids, inspect brew specs, and serve customer tickets.

levels.title: The Golden Ratio
levels.goal: Dose 18.0g of coffee into the portafilter and extract a 36.0g double shot in 27 to 30 seconds.
levels.instruction: Walk to the Dosing & Grinder Bench, adjust grind size and dose, then pull your double espresso shot at the Espresso Machine.
customerProfiles: A regular requesting an espresso double with clean acidity and balanced sweetness
actions: Tare scale and weigh dry coffee dose
Adjust grind fineness collar
Distribute grounds with WDT tool and tamp at 15kg pressure
Flush grouphead for 2 seconds
Lock portafilter and engage brew pump
successConditions: Tamp is verified level without channeling
Extraction duration completes between 27 and 30 seconds
steps: Weigh ground coffee dose to 18.0g using precision scale
Set grinder collar to optimal espresso range (2.2 - 2.5)
Engage WDT distribution and level tamp into 58mm basket
Flush grouphead, engage portafilter immediately, and stop shot at 36g
checks: Check that portafilter basket is dry and preheated
Verify 9 bar pump gauge pressure during flow
Confirm no spritzing from bottomless portafilter
Check shot timer matches target recipe window

levels.title: Velvet Vortex
levels.goal: Steam whole milk into glossy, silky microfoam at 60°C to 65°C without large surface bubbles.
levels.instruction: Walk to the Milk Steaming Station, purge the steam wand, stretch milk for 4 seconds, swirl into a vortex, and stop at 63°C.
customerProfiles: A flat white enthusiast expecting wet-paint texture milk at drinking temperature
actions: Retrieve cold milk from fridge and fill pitcher to spout notch
Purge condensation from steam wand
Submerge steam tip 1cm and introduce air hiss for stretching
Tilt pitcher to create whirlpool vortex for integration
Shut off steam valve at target temp, wipe wand, and purge
successConditions: Steam wand is purged before immersion and wiped/purged after shutoff
Aeration period is maintained between 3.5s and 5.0s
Vortex angle is maintained between 25° and 35° for homogeneous texture
Final milk temperature settles between 60°C and 65°C
steps: Pour 200ml cold whole milk into cold 350ml stainless pitcher
Purge steam wand into damp cloth to clear condensation
Submerge tip slightly below surface, open valve full, stretch for 4 seconds
Sink wand tip deeper, maintain rolling vortex until thermometer reads 60°C, then shut off
Clean wand and tap pitcher on bench to collapse stray bubbles
checks: Confirm no high-pitched screeching during aeration
Inspect milk surface for shiny wet-paint gloss
Ensure milk temperature does not exceed 68°C scald threshold
Verify steam wand is completely clean with no dried milk residue

levels.title: Canvas in a Cup
levels.goal: Integrate espresso crema with microfoam and execute a centered 3-tier tulip latte art design.
levels.instruction: Walk to the Service Counter with your freshly pulled shot and textured milk, set pour height and angle, and complete the tulip pour.
customerProfiles: A specialty café patron ordering an in-house ceramic cup Latte
actions: Swirl espresso to break surface tension and blend crema
Tilt ceramic cup 45 degrees toward pitcher
Pour pencil-thin stream from 8cm height to establish liquid canvas base
Bring pitcher spout down to 1cm above surface to deposit white foam stacks
Cut through pattern with elevated thin stream from base to tip
successConditions: Initial cup tilt is set between 40° and 45°
Base canvas poured from 7.0cm to 9.0cm without prematurely marking crema
Pattern foam deposited at close proximity (0.5cm - 1.5cm)
Final cup symmetry and contrast score exceeds 85%
steps: Swirl espresso and polished milk to homogenize
Pour thin stream from 8cm height in circular motion to fill cup half-full without marking
Lower pitcher spout right against surface and increase flow rate to wrap white foam
Push forward, deposit second and third tier stacks while leveling cup
Lift pitcher 6cm and draw thin stream forward to complete center strike
checks: Verify sharp brown/white color contrast along cup rim
Inspect symmetry across the central axis of the cup
Ensure cup is filled to exactly 3mm below rim without spillage
Confirm no bubble clusters on top design

levels.title: Morning Rush Hour
levels.goal: Coordinate grinder, steam wand, and espresso station to craft an Oat Cortado and an Iced Americano within 90 seconds.
levels.instruction: Walk between stations to grind consecutive doses, steam alternative milk, and deliver both orders to the Service Counter before the timer runs out.
customerProfiles: A commuter needing a quick to-go Iced Americano
A local designer ordering a dine-in Oat Milk Cortado with silky texture
actions: Read ticket sequence and queue drink prep order
Fill cold cup with 180g ice and 150ml filtered cold water
Grind and pull shot 1 over ice for Iced Americano
Grind and pull shot 2 into cortado glass
Steam 120ml oat milk to 58°C and pour 1:1 ratio cortado
Place both finished drinks on service counter ticket trays

controls.label: Prep Sequencing Order
controls.default: Americano Water First -> Pull Shots Back to Back -> Steam Oat Milk
options: Steam Oat Milk First -> Pull Both Shots -> Add Ice Later
Americano Water First -> Pull Shots Back to Back -> Steam Oat Milk
Pull Cortado Shot First -> Steam Milk -> Pull Americano Shot -> Add Ice

successConditions: Correct workflow sequence selected to minimize shot oxidation
Oat milk temperature kept strictly between 55°C and 60°C to avoid curdling
Cortado prepared at strict 1:1 ratio with velvety texture
Station wiped and portafilters knocked out upon delivery
steps: Prepare cold cup with ice and cold water at service counter
Dose and lock first basket, start extraction directly over cold water base
Dose second basket immediately, extract double shot into cortado glass
Steam cold oat milk to 58°C, texturing gently for low volume pitcher
Pour cortado to rim, cap Americano, clear portafilters, and ring ticket
checks: Confirm Iced Americano crema crown is preserved over cold water
Confirm oat milk is smooth without curdling or phase separation
Verify all portafilters rinsed and re-locked into heated groups
